{{Quote|Just remember&ndash;tell your friends! Tell your enemies! I stand behind all my products! One-hundred-percent pure, satisfaction guaranteed!|Elan Sel'Sabagno to Boba Fett|<ref name="Boba Fett: Pursuit">''[[Boba Fett: Pursuit]]''</ref>}}
'''Elan Sel'Sabagno''', also known as '''Elan Sleazebaggano''', was a [[Balosar (species)/Legends|Balosar]] [[Gender/Legends|male]] medical student who came to the [[Planet/Legends|planet]] [[Coruscant/Legends|Coruscant]] seeking out a medical degree. However, he fell in with a bad crowd and stole medical supplies and equipment, which he gave to the [[spice lord]] [[Hat Lo/Legends|Hat Lo]]. Sel'Sabagno eventually stole drug supplies to give to him and became a [[Spice/Legends|spice]] [[Drug dealer|dealer]] and [[Slythmonger/Legends|slythmonger]]. A best-seller of his were [[Death stick/Legends|death sticks]], drugs that shortened the life of the user. Sel'Sabagno himself became addicted to death sticks, though his Balosar physiology gave him resistance to the drug. The death sticks sold at the [[Outlander Club/Legends|Outlander Club]] located in the [[Uscru Entertainment District/Legends|Uscru Entertainment District]] of Coruscant.

While at the club in [[22 BBY/Legends|22 BBY]], Sel'Sabagno tried to sell [[Rancor nail blade]]s to [[Bounty hunter/Legends|bounty hunter]] [[Jango Fett/Legends|Jango Fett]], though Fett refused and pushed him aside. Shortly after in that same [[Standard year/Legends|year]], Sel'Sabagno tried to sell death sticks to [[Jedi Knight/Legends|Jedi Knight]] [[Obi-Wan Kenobi/Legends|Obi-Wan Kenobi]]. Kenobi, however, used the [[The Force/Legends|Force]] to [[Mind trick/Legends|mind trick]] the slythmonger into going home and rethinking his life. He exited the club and changed his ways for a [[Time/Legends|time]].

In [[19 BBY/Legends|19 BBY]], Sel'Sabagno drove the bounty hunter [[Boba Fett/Legends|Boba Fett]] in an [[Airspeeder/Legends|airspeeder]] from the [[Jedi Temple/Legends|Jedi Temple]] to the [[Sign of the Tri-Forked Tongue]] cantina on the orders of Hat Lo. During the drive, the slythmonger tried to sell many products to Fett and endangered their lives by poorly driving his speeder. After Fett finished his business in the cantina, Sel'Sabagno drove the bounty hunter back to the Jedi Temple. On the way there, he gave Fett a [[Kaminoan/Legends|Kaminoan]] [[Mk I Saberdart/Legends|saberdart]] of unknown origin. After the rise of the [[Galactic Empire/Legends|Galactic Empire]], Sel'Sabgano unsuccessfully tried to inform the Jedi fugitives [[Drake Lo'gaan/Legends|Drake Lo'gaan]] and [[Zonder/Legends|Zonder]] of the dangers of death stick usage.

==Biography==
===A once promising career===
[[File:Coruscant-EotE.jpg|thumb|right|300px|Elan Sel'Sabagno came to the planet Coruscant (pictured).]]
The young [[Balosar (species)/Legends|Balosar]] Elan Sel'Sabagno, known to almost everyone as Elan Sleazebaggano,<ref name="Gamer10">{{GamerCite|10|Galactic Power Brokers}}</ref> was a medical student<ref name="CSWE">{{CSWECite|III|168|Sleazebaggano, Elan}}</ref> who came to<ref name="FF" /> the [[Core Worlds/Legends|Core Worlds]] [[Planet/Legends|planet]]<ref name="Complete Locations">[[Star Wars: Complete Locations (2005)|''Star Wars: Complete Locations'']]</ref> [[Coruscant/Legends|Coruscant]]<ref name="FF" /> seeking out a medical degree<ref name="Gamer10" /> as one of the top students in his [[Standard year/Legends|year]]. He studied on the planet,<ref name="DB" /> which was now his [[Homeworld/Legends|home]],<ref name="Character Encyclopedia" /> and had a place in medical school with a promising career ahead of him. However, the popular Coruscant view that Balosars were untrustworthy dragged him down. His ancestry attracted the wrong type of attention and the Balosar fell in with the wrong crowd.<ref name="FF" /> 

Before Sel'Sabagno knew where he was, he was stealing medical equipment<ref name="FF" /> and supplies<ref name="Gamer10" /> from his university's stores, which he passed off to the<ref name="FF" /> up-and-coming<ref name="Gamer10" /> [[spice lord]] [[Hat Lo/Legends|Hat Lo]]. The [[Galactic Credit Standard/Legends|credits]] he received helped with hard student life, and he soon went to stealing valuable drug supplies to give to Lo, accelerating his slippery path towards dark [[Standard day/Legends|days]].<ref name="FF" /> When one of Sel'Sabagno's [[Elan Sel'Sabagno's instructor|instructors]] accused him of stealing, the Balosar assaulted the instructor and went into hiding in the labyrinth-like [[Coruscant Underworld/Legends|undercities]] of Coruscant.<ref name="Gamer10" />

Sel'Sabagno had turned his medical career into the career of a [[Slythmonger/Legends|slythmonger]], a distributor of pharmaceutical supplies in the entertainment districts of Coruscant.<ref name="DB" /> He also became a small-time criminal,<ref name="Jedi">[[Star Wars: I Want to Be a Jedi (2007)|''Star Wars: I Want to Be a Jedi'']]</ref> and a barfly who engaged in the seedier side of Coruscant nightlife.<ref name="CSWE" /> Sel'Sabagno frequented shadowy nightclubs in the [[Uscru Entertainment District/Legends|Uscru Entertainment District]] of Coruscant<ref name="ToppsEvo" /> and dealt the drug [[Spice/Legends|Spice]].<ref name="Galactic Files">{{Topps|set=2013 Topps Star Wars Galactic Files Series 2|cardname=Elan Sleazebaggano (Spice Dealer)|link=https://www.tcdb.com/ViewCard.cfm/sid/93283/cid/6569382/2013-Topps-Star-Wars:-Galactic-Files-Series-2-357-Elan-Sleazebaggano}}</ref> The Balosar was able to put his rudimentary medical training to use behind the bar of a seedy nightclub. He found that after a few drinks, it was easy to over-charge patrons or talk them into buying the drug [[Glitterstim/Legends|glitterstim]] or<ref name="Gamer10" /> his best seller,<ref name="DB" /> [[Death stick/Legends|death sticks]], which he peddled to Hat Lo. The slythmonger had also turned into a death stick addict himself and shared the drugs with his coterie of thrill-seeking club hoppers.<ref name="Gamer10" /> The death sticks sold at the [[Outlander Club/Legends|Outlander Club]],<ref name="FF" /> a [[Nightclub/Legends|nightclub]] and [[Gambling/Legends|gambling]] hall in the Uscru Entertainment District,<ref name="CSWE2">{{CSWECite|II|431|Outlander Club}}</ref> due to their quality. As such, the customers of the club tolerated him despite the fact he was a deadly blot on it.<ref name="FF" /> He loitered around the bar of the club looking for potential customers.<ref name="FF96">{{FactFile|96|OUT 1-2|Outlander Nightclub Patrons}}</ref>

===Outlander encounters===
{{Quote|You wanna buy some death sticks?"<br />"You don't want to sell me death sticks.''"<br />"''I don't wanna sell you death sticks.''"<br />"''You want to go home and rethink your life.''"<br />"''I wanna go home and rethink my life.|Elan Sel'Sabagno and Obi-Wan Kenobi, in which the latter uses a mind trick on the former|<ref name="Episode 2" />}}
[[File:WannaBuyNails.png|thumb|left|250px|Sel'Sabagno attempts to sell Rancor nail blades to Jango Fett.]]
In [[22 BBY/Legends|22 BBY]],<ref name="NEC Note">''[[The New Essential Chronology]]'' dates the events of [[Star Wars: Episode II Attack of the Clones|''Star Wars'': Episode II ''Attack of the Clones'']] to [[22 BBY/Legends|22 BBY]]. The scene from ''[[Jango Fett: Bounty Hunter]]'' in which Elan Sel'Sabagno offers [[Rancor nail blade]]s to [[Jango Fett/Legends|Jango Fett]] takes place shortly before the film's [[Plot to assassinate Senator Amidala/Legends|assassination attempt]] on [[Senator/Legends|Senator]] [[Padmé Amidala/Legends|Padmé Amidala]].</ref> Sel'Sabagno visited the Outlander Club at the same time as the [[Bounty hunter/Legends|bounty hunters]] [[Jango Fett/Legends|Jango Fett]] and [[Zam Wesell/Legends|Zam Wesell]]. He attempted to sell [[Rancor nail blade]]s, weapons crafted from the nails of [[Rancor/Legends|Rancors]], to Fett, blocking Wesell's way. The bounty hunter refused, pushing Sel'Sabagno aside and making him stumble backwards into a table of [[Droid/Legends|droids]].<ref name="Jango Fett: Bounty Hunter">''[[Jango Fett: Bounty Hunter]]''</ref>

During a [[Local day/Legends|night]]<ref name="Episode 2" /> shortly after,<ref name="NEC Note" /> Sel'Sabagno was once again in the club, sitting at the bar and interacting with<ref name="Episode 2" /> chief [[Bartender/Legends|bartender]] [[Bufon Taire/Legends|Bufon Taire]]<ref name="Who's Who">{{InsiderCite|75|Who's Who in the Outlander Club: It's Ladies' Night}}</ref> when the [[Jedi/Legends|Jedi]] [[Obi-Wan Kenobi/Legends|Obi-Wan Kenobi]] and [[Anakin Skywalker/Legends|Anakin Skywalker]] entered the club searching for Wesell after her [[Plot to assassinate Senator Amidala/Legends|assassination attempt]] on [[Senator/Legends|Senator]] [[Padmé Amidala/Legends|Padmé Amidala]]. With a death stick in hand, he approached the Kenobi at the bar,<ref name="Episode 2">{{Film|II}}</ref> thinking he was a visiting patron,<ref name="ToppsEvo">{{Topps|set=2006 Topps Star Wars Evolution: Update Edition|cardname=Elan Sleazebaggano|link=https://www.tcdb.com/ViewCard.cfm/sid/75303/cid/5906312/2006-Topps-Star-Wars:-Evolution-Update-Edition-23-Elan-Sleazebaggano}}</ref> and attempted to sell him death sticks.<ref name="Episode 2" /> To any respectable person, the Balosar would have been an annoyance, but to Kenobi, he was just an unwelcome distraction. The Jedi didn't want Sel'Sabagno to be put in danger or peddle his wares elsewhere, so Kenobi, keeping his eyes forward, did a slight gesture<ref name="Life and Legend" /> of influence<ref name="aotcvis" /> with his hand and [[Mind trick/Legends|mind-tricked]] the slythmonger into not selling his death sticks to him.<ref name="Life and Legend">''[[The Life and Legend of Obi-Wan Kenobi]]''</ref> Sel'Sabagno then used a slight of hand<ref name="Alienation">{{InsiderCite|70|Alienation: The Aliens of Episode II}}</ref> to tuck the death stick into the sleeve of his [[Clothing/Legends|overcoat]].<ref name="Episode 2" />

[[File:Sleazebaggano_mind_tricked.png|thumb|right|400px|Elan Sel'Sabagno was mind tricked by Obi-Wan Kenobi.]]
Sel'Sabagno was unaware that the Jedi was manipulating his mind. He appeared slightly confused, then thoughtful as he<ref name="Life and Legend/> obediently<ref name="Novelization" /> responded that he didn't want to sell death sticks to Kenobi. The Jedi then again mind-tricked him into going home and rethinking his life. The Balosar left his drink behind and walked away from the bar.<ref name="Life and Legend" /> He exited the club, walking along [[Vos Gesal Street/Legends|Vos Gesal Street]] back to his home to rethink his life.<ref name="Complete Locations" /> 

Kenobi's trick of the force led him to better things, though he never knew where the inspiration to change came from. All Sel'Sabagno knew was that he attempted to sell death sticks to a punter and left the club, never returning.<ref name="FF" /> He saw the error of his criminal ways<ref name="Galactic Files" /> and led an honest life,<ref name="Jedi" /> though only briefly.<ref name="Galactic Files" /> The interaction became famous<ref name="Galactic Files" /> and rumors about Sel'Sabagno going home and changing his ways circulated.<ref name="ToppsEvo" /> Unfortunately for the Outlander Club, more slythmongers were there to take Sel'Sabagno's place.<ref name="FF" /> At some point following his Outlander visit, Skywalker drew the Balosar alongside<ref name="Journal">''[[Anakin Skywalker: A Jedi's Journal]]''</ref> the [[Twi'lek/Legends|Twi'lek]] woman [[Ayy Vida/Legends|Ayy Vida]]<ref name="Who's Who" /> in his journal and dubbed them "local lowlifes."<ref name="Journal" />

===Driving Boba Fett===
====The pickup====
{{Quote|Oh no! Not Elan Sleazebaggano!<br />Elan's the name, flying's my game! Unless I could interest you in some Polordion smootdust?|Boba Fett and Elan Sel'Sabagno|<ref name="Boba Fett: Pursuit">''[[Boba Fett: Pursuit]]''</ref>}}
[[File:Jedi_Temple_spires_ROTS.png|thumb|left|300px|Sel'Sabagno picked up Boba Fett from the Jedi Temple.]]
In [[19 BBY/Legends|19 BBY]],<ref name="TERC">''[[The Essential Reader's Companion]]'' dates the events of ''[[Boba Fett: Pursuit]]'' to [[19 BBY/Legends|19 BBY]].</ref> Lo sent Sel'Sabagno in an [[Airspeeder/Legends|airspeeder]] to pick up [[Boba Fett/Legends|Boba Fett]], the bounty hunter child of Jango Fett, from the [[Jedi Temple/Legends|Jedi Temple]] on Coruscant, and bring him to his [[Cantina/Legends|cantina]], [[Sign of the Tri-Forked Tongue]] in the Coruscant underworld. Fett and Lo were to conduct business there, the former seeking weapons for his planned confrontation with [[Jedi Master/Legends|Jedi Master]] [[Mace Windu/Legends|Mace Windu]]. Sel'Sabagno waited for Fett inside his airspeeder near Fett's ship, the ''[[Slave I/Legends|Slave I]]'', on the landing dock of the temple. Fett immediately recognized the Balosar as being Sel'Sabagno, to his dismay.<ref name="Boba Fett: Pursuit" />

As Fett jumped into the airspeeder, Sel'Sabagno introduced himself, his [[Antennapalps/Legends|antennapalps]] wiggling with pride. He told Fett that "flying was his game" and asked Fett if he could interest him in some [[Polordion smootdust]]. Sel'Sabagno took out the smootdust, and waved it enticingly around Fett's face. Fett then grabbed Sel'Sabagno's shoulder and told him that he wasn't interested in his cheap contraband. He then instructed the Balosar to take him the Sign of the Tri-Forked Tongue fast. Sel'Sabagno nodded eagerly and the smootdust disappeared. Sel'Sabagno punched the control panels of the airspeeder and it left the docking platform.<ref name="Boba Fett: Pursuit" />

The Balosar commented that Fett looked like a discerning bounty hunter, and almost without taking a breath, offered to sell him [[tortapo]]-shell shades. He went on about the features of the shades before Fett ordered him to be silent and tightened his grip on his shoulder. Sel'Sabagno agreed, with his antennapalps twitching nervously. Even after Fett's order, Sel'Sabagno continued to go on. Fett groaned and thought to himself that the Balosar was relentless and wondered where his blaster was when he needed it. The bounty hunter menacingly stated that the trip better be short and Sel'Sabagno obliged. The airspeeder then raced away from the temple.<ref name="Boba Fett: Pursuit" />

====The drop-off====
{{Quote|I happen to be the provider of the very finest death sticks in the galaxy, very reasonably priced, very&ndash;"<br />"Stop! Get me to the Tri-Forked Tongue. NOW!|Elan Sel'Sabagno and Boba Fett|<ref name="Boba Fett: Pursuit" />}} 
[[File:BobaFettFull-OP.png|thumb|right|250px|Sel'Sabagno drove Boba Fett (pictured) to the Sign of the Tri-Forked Tongue.]]
As the two approached the [[Senate Building/Legends|Galactic Senate Building]], Sel'Sabagno explained to Fett that the building is where [[The galaxy/Legends|the galaxy]]'s most important business takes place, but before he could explain where they were going, the airspeeder gave a sudden lurch and, without warning, dived straight down between [[Kilometer/Legends|kilometer]]-high buildings. The bounty hunter shouted at the Balosar as another speeder came towards them. At the last moment, Fett got the airspeeder to veer sharply to one side. Fett caught a glimpse of the angry pilot's face of the other speeder, glaring at Sel'Sabagno's bright red one. The Balosar then calmly removed Fett's hand from the airspeeder's controls.<ref name="Boba Fett: Pursuit" />

Sel'Sabagno then continued his speech, stating that the Coruscant underground is where the galaxy's most important unofficial business takes place. Fett then corrected him, stating that he was talking about the gangland underground. The airspeeder sped down into the lower levels of Coruscant's Galactic City, which Fett called Hat Lo's territory. Sel'Sabagno then retorted that it was also his territory, and that he sold the finest, reasonably priced death sticks in the galaxy. Before he could finish, Fett shouted at him to stop and to get him to the cantina.<ref name="Boba Fett: Pursuit" />

The rest of the ride passed silently, with Sel'Sabagno occasionally sighing noisily. His antennapalps didn't stop wriggling as though he was trying to sell Fett some highly illegal one hundred percent pure [[Nkllonian lava extract|Nkllonian Lava Extract]]. At last, the airspeeder began to slow, and in front of them was the Sign of the Tri-Forked Tongue. A bored sounding Sel'Sabagno announced the name of the establishment to Fett. Sel'Sabagno told the bounty hunter he didn't know why the bounty hunter bothered with the place, adding that no one visited anymore. Fett snapped that he did and exited the airspeeder. The Balosar handed him his business card, asking Fett to call him when Lo is unable to provide him with what the bounty hunter needed. Boba added that contacting him was unlikely, but he still took the card. The airspeeder then roared off, wildly moving between alarmed passersby.<ref name="Boba Fett: Pursuit" />

===The drive back===
{{Quote|Yo! Wassup!|Elan Sel'Sabagno to Boba Fett|<ref name="Boba Fett: Pursuit" />}}
After Boba Fett had acquired his weapons from Hat Lo in the cantina, Sel'Sabagno and his airspeeder hovered near the buildings entrance. He gestured for Fett to hop in beside him. The dismayed bounty hunter looked around, seeing no other means of transportation. Sel'Sabagno urged Fett to get in, telling him that he'll get him there faster than anyone else could. The resigned Fett climbed into the airspeeder, glowering at the Balosar. Fett threatened Sel'Sabagno with death if he tried to sell something to him. Sel'Sabagno yanked the controls and airspeeder shot up through the high-rises of Coruscant. The Balosar told Fett he wouldn't dream of selling him something, especially not something highly illegal and fatality toxic like a [[Mk I Saberdart/Legends|saberdart]],<ref name="Boba Fett: Pursuit" /> a fork-shaped toxic dart from the planet [[Kamino/Legends|Kamino]].<ref name="KaminoSaberdart">{{DB|technology|kaminosaberdart|Kamino saberdart}}</ref>

[[File:KaminoSaberdart-BHC.png|thumb|left|200px|Sel'Sabagno posessed a saberdart.]]
Holding tightly to his seat as the airspeeder narrowly avoided hitting a building, Fett inquired about the saberdart. Sel'Sabagno stated he never said anything about a saberdart, before waving at a speeder going past them full of young, willowy [[Witches of Dathomir|Dathomir witches]]. The witches stared back at him with ill-disguised disgust. The speeder shot upwards as Sel'Sabagno replied that possessing a saberdart is a criminal offense, and that he, of course, is a respected member of Corsucant's business community. The Balosar took one hand from the controls and materialized a saberdart from what seemed like thin air. The airspeeder wobbled dangerously while doing so. He gave the saberdart to Fett as a token of his great admiration for his great bounty hunting skills, and added on that Fett should put in a good word for the Balosar to the<ref name="Boba Fett: Pursuit" /> [[Hutt/Legends|Hutt]] [[Crime lord/Legends|crime lord]]<ref name="Jabba">{{FactFile|38|JAB 1-4|Jabba the Hutt}}</ref> [[Jabba Desilijic Tiure/Legends|Jabba Desilijic Tiure]], if he felt inclined. Fett took the saberdart, looking at it suspiciously. Fett tried to inquire about where he got the saberdart, but was cut off. Sel'Sabagno stated if he did tell Fett where he got it, the bounty hunter would kill him, adding that it was real, and that Fett should trust him.<ref name="Boba Fett: Pursuit" />

As they approached the Jedi Temple, the airspeeder began to slow. Fett quickly shoved the saberdart into his [[Utility belt/Legends|utility belt]] and the airspeeder came to a stop on the landing platform. Fett exited the airspeeder and grudgingly thanked the Balosar. Sel'Sabagno looked up at Fett and wriggled his antennapalps. He told Fett to remember to tell his friends, and his enemies, that he stands behind his products, one-hundred-percent pure, satisfaction guaranteed. With a farewell wave of his antennapalps, Sel'Sabagno powered up his airspeeder, shooting in reverse. It rocketed off into the haze of Coruscant as Fett watched it go.<ref name="Boba Fett: Pursuit" />

===The dangers of death sticks===
{{Quote|They call them "death sticks" for a reason...|Elan Sel'Sabagno|<ref name="ea:r">''[[Evasive Action: Recruitment]]''</ref>}}
Shortly after the rise of the [[Galactic Empire/Legends|Galactic Empire]]<ref name="Hyperspace">{{InsiderCite|85|Best of Hyperspace}}</ref> in 19 BBY,<ref name="NECRotS">''[[The New Essential Chronology]]'' dates the events of {{Film|III}} to [[19 BBY/Legends|19 BBY]].</ref> Sel'Sabagno attempted to tell the Jedi fugitives [[Drake Lo'gaan/Legends|Drake Lo'gaan]] and [[Zonder/Legends|Zonder]] about the dangers of death sticks<ref name="ea:r" /> on Vos Gesal Street<ref name="Complete Locations" /> after they ran out of the Outlander Club from [[Stormtrooper/Legends|Stormtroopers]]. The pair didn't acknowledge Sel'Sabagno and pushed him out the way, hurting him. The unsuccessful Balosar then remarked that he needed to rethink his life.<ref name="ea:r" />

==Personality and traits==
{{Quote|I live to please. But maybe, you'll consider&ndash;''"<br />"''[Boba groans]|Elan Sel'Sabagno and Boba Fett|<ref name="Boba Fett: Pursuit" />}}
[[File:Elan_Sleazebaggano.png|thumb|right|250px|Elan Sel'Sabagno was a sordid and slimy Balosar.]]
Being a sordid<ref name="H2H" /> and slimy lowlife,<ref name="Character Encyclopedia" /> Sel'Sabagno didn't care that other species couldn't shrug off the effects of death sticks,<ref name="Gamer10" /> though by the time of the Galactic Empire he tried to spread awareness of the drug's harmful nature to Lo'gaan and Zondar.<ref name="ea:r" /> Sel'Sabagno did nothing to dispel the stereotypes that Balosars were scoundrels and shifty cheats.<ref name="DB" /> Though he thought that his oily style, embarrassing dance moves, and occasional sleights of hand, which he learned during his time with a troupe of trickster players, brought him popularity, only the quality of his Death sticks made him popular in the seedy Coruscant scene.<ref name="scrapbook">''[[Star Wars: Attack of the Clones Scrapbook]]''</ref> In actuality, the clubbers viewed him as an awkward, oily, embarrassing parasite.<ref name="DB" /> When introducing himself to Boba Fett, the<ref name="Boba Fett: Pursuit" /> notorious<ref name="Character Encyclopedia" /> slythmonger's antennapalps wiggled in pride. He also referred to himself as a "respected member of Coruscant's business community" to Fett.<ref name="Boba Fett: Pursuit" />

Sel'Sabagno was addicted to death sticks, drugs that shorted the user's lifespan. However, his Balosar physiology gave him a heightened resistance to the more damaging side effects of the drug.<ref name="DB" /> Despite his physiology, years of hard living in the undercity of Coruscant had weakened his health.<ref name="H2H" /> A sweaty, hollow-eyed<ref name="FF71">{{FactFile2014|71|SLE 1-2|Elan Sel'Sabagno}}</ref> [[Gender/Legends|male]] of the Balosar [[Species/Legends|species]],<ref name="DB" /> he had flexible antennapalps<ref name="aotcvis">''[[Star Wars: Attack of the Clones: The Visual Dictionary]]''</ref> that twirled up from his head like curly horns.<ref name="Novelization">[[Star Wars: Episode II Attack of the Clones (novelization)|''Star Wars'': Episode II ''Attack of the Clones'' novelization]]</ref> He could conceal the antennapalps with<ref name="aotcvis" /> his thick [[Color/Legends|brown]] hair,<ref name="FF" /> worn in a stylishly filthy<ref name="Life and Legend" /> petrified hairstyle.<ref name="aotcvis" /> He also had brown [[Eye/Legends|eyes]], and light skin. He stood at 1.78 [[Meter/Legends|meters]]<ref name="FF" /> (5 [[Foot/Legends|feet]], 10 inches)<ref name="Character Encyclopedia" /> and weighed 70 [[Kilogram/Legends|kilograms]].<ref name="H2H" /> The Balosar spoke with a guttural voice<ref name="Novelization" /> and was affiliated with the [[Galactic Republic]].<ref name="Character Encyclopedia" />

==Skills and abilities==
Sel'Sabagno was one of the top medical students within his year.<ref name="FF" /> The slythmonger was knowledgeable on many subjects, including [[Alien/Legends|alien]] species, biology, and organized crime.<ref name="Gamer10" /> His rudimentary knowledge of alien psychology was used to hustle contraband.<ref name="scrapbook" /> He had some skill with gathering information and [[Computer/Legends|computer]] use.<ref name="Gamer10" /> Sel'Sabagno had slightly above average intelligence, speed, and diplomacy skills, below-average strength, and low fighting ability.<ref name="Galactic Files" /> With little combat experience, his fighting style was deliberately clumsy and unpredictable,<ref name="H2H" /> though he did have proficiency with [[Blaster pistol/Legends|blaster pistols]] and simple weapons.<ref name="Gamer10" /> As he was a Balosar, he had his species' natural immunoresistance to industrial pollutants and [[Poison/Legends|toxins]], and an otherworldly sense of hearing.<ref name="Alienation" /> 

Sel'Sabagno could speak and write [[Balosur]],<ref name="Gamer10" /> the language of his species.<ref name="UAA">''[[Ultimate Alien Anthology]]''</ref> He could also speak in [[Galactic Basic Standard/Legends|Basic]], [[Huttese/Legends|Huttese]], and [[Twi'leki/Legends|Twi'leki]].<ref name="Gamer10" /> During his time with a troupe of trickster players, he learned how to do slights of hand,<ref name="scrapbook" /> becoming an adept.<ref name="Alienation" /> According to Sel'Sabagno, "flying was his game" but while using an airspeeder, he put himself and Boba Fett in danger many times.<ref name="Boba Fett: Pursuit" /> He was not [[Force-sensitive/Legends|Force-sensitive]].<ref name="Galactic Files" />

==Equipment==
{{Quote|I never said that, because to possess a saberdart is a criminal offence. and I, of course, am a respected member of Coruscant's business community. But yes, I do have one.|Elan Sel'Sabagno to Boba Fett|<ref name="Boba Fett: Pursuit" />}}
[[File:Deathsticks-DB.png|thumb|left|200px|Sel'Sabagno sold death sticks.]]
On multiple occasions<ref name="Jango Fett: Bounty Hunter" /><ref name="Episode 2" /><ref name="ea:r" /> starting from 22 BBY,<ref name="NEC Note" /> Sel'Sabagno wore a long dark overcoat that concealed his illegal chemicals, a casual beige shirt, baggy white pants,<ref name="Character Encyclopedia" /> a black belt with a [[Holster/Legends|holster]],<ref name="Figure">{{HasbroCite|set=Star Wars (Hasbro toy line)|packtype='03 Basic Figure|pack=#40: Elan Sleazebaggano (Outlander Nightclub Encounter)|altlink=https://www.rebelscum.com/sw0340sleazebaggano.asp}}</ref> a fashionable choker, and shoes that contained secret storage compartments for contraband.<ref name="Character Encyclopedia" /> Sel'Sabagno also possessed a blaster pistol,<ref name="Figure" /> a sharp [[Vibroblade/Legends|vibroblade]],<ref name="H2H" /> multiple Rancor nail blades,<ref name="Jango Fett: Bounty Hunter">''[[Jango Fett: Bounty Hunter]]''</ref> flashy clothes, and a stash of illegal substances that included [[Ryll/Legends|ryll spice]], glitterstim, and death sticks.<ref name="Gamer10" /> 

By 19 BBY,<ref name="TERC" /> Sel'Sabagno had come into possession of a saberdart, which he could not reveal the origin of, for fear of being killed by Boba Fett. Other material he had at this time included tortapo-shell shades and the shimmering green Polordian smootdust, which he called "one hundred percent pure" before being cut off by Fett. He utilized a bright red airspeeder when driving around Fett. After exiting the airspeeder, Sel'Sabagno gave Fett a business card. On the card read "''ELAN SLEAZEBAGGNO: WHEN ONLY THE BEST AND SLIMIEST WILL DO!''"<ref name="Boba Fett: Pursuit" />

==Behind the scenes==
===Creation===
{{Quote|Elan Sleazebaggano was altered in postproduction, too late for toys in the works to change. The proper Elan has no ears. Reference photography didn't have this digital alteration. Toys had a running change to remove his ears.|[[Pablo Hidalgo]]|<ref name="Hidalgo tweet #2">{{Twitter|pablohidalgo|status/981652528931549186|[[Pablo Hidalgo]]|quote=Today's Star Wars Show reminds me: Elan Sleazebaggano was altered in postproduction, too late for toys in the works to change. The proper Elan has no ears. Reference photography didn't have this digital alteration. Toys had a running change to remove his ears.|archivefile=File:HidalgoSleazebaggano.png}}</ref>}}
[[File:ElanSleazebagganoConcept.jpg|thumb|right|250px|Concept art of Elan Sel'Sabagno]]
Elan Sel'Sabagno was created<ref name="Power1" /> for the [[prequel trilogy]] film [[Star Wars: Episode II Attack of the Clones|''Star Wars'': Episode II ''Attack of the Clones'']],<ref name="Episode 2" /> released on [[May 16]], [[2002]].<ref name="Year">''[[Star Wars Year By Year: A Visual History, New Edition]]''</ref> The character was named by ''[[Star Wars]]'' creator [[George Lucas]]<ref name="Hidalgo tweet #1">{{Twitter|pablohidalgo|status/981665660496302080|[[Pablo Hidalgo]]|quote=George Lucas did.|archivefile=File:HidalgoSleazebaggano.png}} {{C|in response to "''I just wanna know who it was that came up with that ''[Elan Sleazebaggano's]'' name.''"}}</ref> and concept art of the character was drawn by concept artist [[Dermot Power]]. One of the designs showed the character as a [[Neimoidian/Legends|Neimoidian]]<ref name="Power2">{{Instagram|username=powerdermot|name=[[Dermot Power]]|url=p/CO13qHZjn0l|date=2021-05-14|quote=‘Sleaze Bagganno’ hooks himself another addict.  Hey Kids - you mustn’t  smoke! ( like vaping but dustier) .  Star Wars Attack of the Clones Coruscant background characters . . .|archivefile=File:DermotPower-Elan Sleazebaggano1-Instagram.png}} {{C|Comment by Power:it was... didn’t look like this though - just a bloke. I remember Thinking ‘please no’ when I was asked to design him . Cringemungus ... but then  I wasn’t the target audience"; in response to: "Wasn’t this a Trade Federation character in the Phantom Menace?"}}</ref> with [[Data goggles/Legends|data goggles]].<ref name=DataGoggles">{{FactFile|123|DAT 1-2|Data Goggles}}</ref> Another piece with the production code "dp400" instead featured him with longer, white hair and no antennapalps. Power labeled the piece as "Sleezebagno".<ref name="Power1">{{Instagram|username=powerdermot|name=[[Dermot Power]]|url=p/BnZCwdaB0-o|date=2018-09-06|quote=Sleezebagno from Episode 2- would probably have been called NickO' Teen if DC hadn't got there first - remember kids ; Never say no to a cigarette!!!|archivefile=File:ElanSleazebaggano-DermotPower-Instagram.png}}</ref> Actor [[Matt Doran]]'s casting as an "unsavory troublemaker" was revealed on [[July 7]], [[2000]] with the publication of the [[StarWars.com]] article "Casting Update: More Local Talent."<ref name="LocalTalent">{{SWArchive|url=episode-ii/bts/production/news20000707.html|text=Casting Update: More Local Talent}}</ref>

Sel'Sabagno was portrayed by Doran<ref name="Episode 2" /> in the Outlander Club scenes shot at [[Fox Studios, Sydney]] on [[July 17]], 2000.<ref name="Mythmaking">''[[Mythmaking: Behind the Scenes of Attack of the Clones]]''</ref> Although Sel'Sabagno has ears in production photos,<ref name="aotcvis" /> [[Industrial Light & Magic]] ultimately removed them and replaced them with antennapalps in postproduction,<ref name="Hidalgo tweet #2" /> carefully matched to Doran's head movements,<ref name="DB" /> for the film after George Lucas saw what computer-graphic antennae looked like.<ref name="Scouting">{{InsiderCite|78|Scouting the Galaxy}}</ref>

===Continuity and appearances===
{{Quote|Nobody’s got better death sticks than Elan Sleazebaggano,|Elan Sel'Sabagno, speaking a line not present in the film in the film's novelization|<ref name="Novelization" />}}
The character was first identified as Elan Sleazebaggano in the "[[Star News]]" department of the [[Star Wars Insider 58|fifty-eighth issue]] of the ''[[Star Wars Insider]]'' magazine, written by [[Scott Chernoff]]<ref name="StarNews">{{InsiderCite|58|Star News}}</ref> and published on [[February 9]], [[2002]].<ref name="SW.com2">{{SWArchive|url=community/news/2002/01/news20020109.html|text=Fan Magazines Cover Episode II}}</ref> The character was later identified with "Sel'Sabagno" in "[[Galactic Power Brokers]]," an article in the [[Star Wars Gamer 10|tenth issue]] of the ''[[Star Wars Gamer]]'' magazine, written by [[J.D. Wiker]]<ref name="Gamer10" /> and released to subscribers on [[April 19]], 2002.<ref name="SW.com">{{SWArchive|url=gaming/other/rpg/news20020416.html|text=Episode II in Gamer #10}}</ref> The film's novelization, written by [[R. A. Salvatore|R.A. Salvatore]]<ref name="Novelization" /> and released on [[April 23]], 2002,<ref name="Cargo Bay">{{RandomHouseOld|url=author/results.pperl?authorid=26771|text=R.A. Salvatore}}</ref> marked the first appearance of the character. The book also adds an extra line of dialogue for Sel'Sabagno not present in the film, where after he asks Kenobi if he wants to buy drugs off of him, he smiles evilly and claims that no one has better death sticks than him.<ref name="Novelization" /> This article assumes the film's version of events is the correct one.

The ''[[Star Wars: Attack of the Clones: The Visual Dictionary]]'' by [[David West Reynolds]]<ref name="aotcvis" /> and also released on April 23 of that year,<ref name="Amazon">{{SWArchive|url=eu/lit/ref/news20020227.html|text=Book Preview: DK Episode II Books}}</ref> reveals that Sel'Sabagno could conceal his antennapalps under his hair,<ref name="aotcvis" /> explaining away photos of the character without the computer-generated effects.<ref name="DB" /> A figure of Sel'Sabagno was produced by the toy company [[Hasbro]] in [[2003]] for their [[Star Wars (Hasbro toy line)|Saga toyline]].<ref name="Toybox">{{InsiderCite|72|Toy Box}}</ref> The figure originally included ears, but a resculpted version without the ears was later produced.<ref name="Scouting2">{{InsiderCite|79|Scouting the Galaxy}}</ref>

===Non-canon and reception===
====Bossk, phone books, and fighting====
{{Quote|&hellip;I heard it was because he was getting ''freaky'' with those Ewoks. You can get away with that in ''some'' systems, but not&mdash;''"<br/>"''&mdash;No, no&mdash;It was the Gungans&hellip;they put a ''hit'' on him. Had enough of his jokes.''"<br/>"''Who hasn't? So what do you know about this new guy ''"Barlow"?''|Elan Sel'Sabagno and Bossk, on the departure of David Land from ''Star Wars Tales''|<ref name="Tales20">{{Tales|20|The Real Life Star Wars Tales Adventures of Jeremy Barlow|The Real Life ''Star Wars Tales'' Adventures of Jeremy Barlow}}</ref>}}
Sel'Sabagno appears in "[[The Real Life Star Wars Tales Adventures of Jeremy Barlow|The Real Life ''Star Wars Tales'' Adventures of Jeremy Barlow]]," a comical story written by [[Jeremy Barlow]] featured in the [[Star Wars Tales 20|twentieth issue]] of ''[[Star Wars Tales]]'',<ref name="Tales20" /> published on [[June 30]], [[2004]].<ref name="TalesRelease">{{DarkHorse|url=Comics/12-583/Star-Wars-Tales-20-Photo-cover|text=Star Wars Tales 20}}</ref> Sel'Sabagno talks with<ref name="Tales20" /> the [[Trandoshan/Legends|Trandoshan]] [[Bounty hunter/Legends|bounty hunter]] [[Bossk/Legends|Bossk]]<ref name="Character Encyclopedia" /> about the departure of editor [[David Land]] from ''Star Wars Tales''. The Balosar puts forth the idea that Land had left because he was getting "freaky" with [[Ewok/Legends|Ewoks]], but Bossk cuts him off and tells him that [[Gungan/Legends|Gungans]] put a hit on him, as they had enough of the jokes made about them. Sel'Sabagno then asks the bounty hunter what he knows about the new addition to Tales, Barlow.<ref name="Tales20" />

In a comical illustration in the "[[Comlink (department)|Comlink]]" department of the [[Star Wars Insider 86|eighty-sixth]] issue of ''Star Wars Insider'',<ref name="Comlink">{{InsiderCite|88|Comlink}}</ref> released on [[June 13]], [[2006]],<ref name="86Date">{{SWArchive|url=community/fanclub/mag/news20060518.html|text=The Sith Rule ''Star Wars Insider'' #88}}</ref> Darth Vader goes through a phonebook with Sel'Sabagno's name and residence on Coruscant in it.<ref name="Comlink" /> 

In the [[2011]] young readers book ''[[Star Wars: Head-to-Head Tag Teams]]'', written by [[Pablo Hidalgo]], a scenario is presented in which Sel'Sabagno is partnered with the identical twin sisters [[Brea Tonnika/Legends|Brea]] and [[Senni Tonnika/Legends|Senni Tonnika]] inside an alley in the Uscru Entertainment District against the [[Con artist/Legends|con artists]] [[Dannl Faytonni/Legends|Dannl Faytonni]] and [[Achk Med-Beq/Legends|Achk Med-Beq]], and the [[Besalisk/Legends|Besalisk]] [[Dexter Jettster/Legends|Dexter Jettster]]. The Experts' Picks section of the book reveals Sel'Sabagno's team loses as he is overpowered and the sisters flee after the odds turn.<ref name="H2H" /> 

====Creators' feelings====
{{Quote|Elan Sleazebaggano bears the most appropriate surname since Marvel Comics' Victor Von Doom. Perhaps his unfortunate appellation led him to his life as a slythmonger, where he peddles "death sticks" to the weak-minded.|Daniel Wallace|<ref name="Who's Who" />}}
[[File:Wallace2-full.jpg|thumb|left|300px|Daniel Wallace (pictured) wrote about Elan Sel'Sabagno within the ''Star Wars Insider'' magazines.]]
"[[Alienation: The Aliens of Episode II]]," an article written by Daniel Wallace and published in the seventieth issue of ''Star Wars Insider''<ref name="Alienation" /> in [[September]] 2003,<ref name="70Release">{{SWArchive|url=community/fanclub/mag/news20030812.html|text=Darth Maul reveals all in ''Insider'' #70}}</ref> Wallace writes that Doran should rethink the lives of both of his characters, Sel'Sabagno and Mouse from<ref name="Alienation" /> the [[1999]] film<ref name="Matrix">{{WebCite|url=https://www.independent.co.uk/arts-entertainment/films/news/star-wars-attack-of-the-clones-hid-an-incredibly-subtle-the-matrix-easter-egg-a6735831.html|text=Star Wars: Attack Of The Clones hid an incredibly subtle The Matrix Easter egg|archivedate=20250316054713}}</ref> ''[[Wikipedia:The Matrix|The Matrix]]''.<ref name="Alienation" /> In "[[Who's Who in the Outlander Club: It's Ladies' Night]]," an article published in the [[Star Wars Insider 75|seventy-fifth issue]] of ''Star Wars Insider''<ref name="Who's Who" /> on [[April 6]], 2004,<ref name="NewFace">{{SWArchive|url=community/fanclub/mag/news20040315.html|text=The New Face of Evil}}</ref> Wallace writes that the characters surname is the most appropriate since the [[Wikipedia:Marvel Comics|Marvel Comics]] character [[Wikipedia:Doctor Doom|Victor Von Doom]]. Wallace also writes that it was perhaps his surname that led him to becoming a slythmonger.<ref name="Who's Who" />

[[John Jackson Miller]], the author of the [[2013]] novel ''[[Kenobi (novel)|Kenobi]]'', revealed that the scene with Sel'Sabagno and Kenobi was one of his favorite scenes of the prequel trilogy in "[[50 Greatest Reasons to Love the Star Wars Prequels!]]," an article written by Mark Newbold and published in the [[Star Wars Insider 147|one hundred fourty-seventh]] issue of ''Star Wars Insider''<ref name="Miller">{{InsiderCite|147|50 Greatest Reasons to Love the Star Wars Prequels!|50 Greatest Reasons to Love the ''Star Wars'' Prequels!|reprint=1}}</ref> on [[January 21]], [[2014]].<ref name="Titan">{{TitanMagazines|url=t/star-wars-insider/us/147|text=Star Wars Insider Issue #147}}</ref> Miller described the scene as a funny off hand moment but added that the watchers are led to wonder how many other people Kenobi and other Jedi have nudged to the right path.<ref name="Miller" />

Dermot Power stated in [[2021]] that he did not like the concept of Sel'Sabagno, calling it cringe, remembered thinking "please no" when asked to design him, and admitted that he wasn't the intended target audience.<ref name="Power2" /> He also later joked that the character would have been named "NickO' Teen" if the name hadn't already been used for [[Wikipedia:Nick O'Teen|a character]] by [[Wikipedia:DC Comics|DC Comics]].<ref name="Power1" />
